Shri Akhlesh Kumar Gupta - Advocate for the appellant
 Shri Arvind Kumar Agrawal- Advocate for respondent No
 Order

This misc. appeal by Claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the Award dated 30/01/2024 passed by learned Ninth Member, MACT, Gwalior (M.P.) in Claim Case No 1308/2022, seeking enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
2. The date of accident, negligence and issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

3. As per the findings of the Tribunal, for the death of Smt. Rashmi (wife of appellant), the Claims Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.10,39,200/- along-with interest in favour of the Claimants under various heads.

4. Learned Counsel for the appellants submits that the Claims Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:20408 2 MA-4188-2024 the case as the amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal is on the lower side.

The Claims Tribunal has committed an error in assessing income of deceased as Rs.3000/- per month instead of Rs.25,000/- per month as per Minimum Wages Act for an house maker, as deceased was having marksheet of 10th, 12th, B.Sc. and PGDCA and she was giving tuition.
Tribunal has awarded future prospects, loss of estate and consortium on lower side.

Hence,
prayed for awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has argued in support of the impugned Award which does not call for any interference by this Court.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of this appeal.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellants.
So far as income of the deceased is concerned, as per the evidence that came on record, her income should be assessed as Rs.9,125/- per month.
Therefore, as per Minimum Wages Act, his income would be fixed as Rs.9,125/- per month instead of Rs.3000/- per month as assessed by the learned Claims Tribunal.

Keeping in view the verdict of the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 , the claimant/appellant is entitled for compensation under the head of future prospects @ 40%.

sentences.text: As regards loss of consortium, appellant is entitled for consortium being the dependents of the deceased and personal expenses i.e. 1/2 of deceased herself should be deducted from her income.

Thus, the compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal is modified as under:-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20408 3 MA-4188-2024 HEAD AMOUNT Annual Income 9,125X12 Rs. 1,09,500/-
 Personal expenses 1/2 Rs. 54,750/--
 Future Prospect 40% Rs. 21,900/-

Total Amount Rs. 76,650/-
 Multiplier "18" 76,650X18 Rs.13,79,700/-
 Loss of Estate Rs. 15,000/-
 Funeral . Rs.15,000/-
 Consortium Rs. 40,000/-
 Total Compensation Amount Rs. 14,49,700/-

Claims Tribunal awarded Rs 10,39,200/-
 Enhanced amount Rs. 4,10,500/-
8.

Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.
14,49,700/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs. 10,39,200/-.

Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs. 4,10,500/- over and above the amount,
which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
9.
In the result, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs. 4,10,500/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
10. With the aforesaid modification, the instant misc. appeal stands disposed of.
